notes: Identity independently checked in canonical text: title Replication of the Superstition and Performance Study by Damisch, Stoberock, and Mussweiler (2010); authors Robert J. Calin-Jageman and Tracy L. Caldwell; DOI 10.1027/1864-9335/a000190; Social Psychology 2014, 45(3):239–245. Primary report with both experiments, methods, results, tables, and references; not abstract-only or preregistration. No PDF supplied; none acquired or rendered. Only assigned unfinished fields populated; other fields are placeholders. Experiment 2 explicitly reports final N = 111 after two exclusions from 113 collected. Internal source discrepancy: Participants and Table 3 note print control n = 54 and superstition-activated n = 66, summing to 120 rather than 111. Retain explicit final N = 111; do not substitute conflicting group sum or infer N from df. Documented flow: 113 - 1 withdrawal - 1 quality-control exclusion = 111; N itself is printed. Requested printed test is t(109) = 0.26 with same-test p = .80; do not substitute before-task luck rating t(96) = 3.65, p = .004, other checks, exploratory subsets, or pooled effect. Conflicting condition counts remain unresolved and require parent review; no numerical correction is made.
